chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: Stuff Smith plays Italian songs outside Petrillo's office
summary: At Local 10, Stuff Smith won his hearing by playing Italian songs in the hall for Petrillo.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: This is February 7th, 1978, and you were about to tell me a story involving Stuff Smith.
Oh, yes, with James Petrillo, when he was -- I don't think he was President of the Federation at that time, but President of Local 10 in Chicago.

And so there were a lot of people that wanted to get into see Petrillo at that time, and Stuff had a kind of goofy -- like he was, he was loose. He wasn't a bad guy, he was just loose and would get into trouble. He would always stumble into trouble. So he knew he had to go see Petrillo, by instinct, and he went to his office and at that time we had a divided local in Chicago. Harry Gray was the President of Local 208, you know.

And Petrillo's the President of Local 10. There were a lot of people outside of Petrillo's office that wanted to see him. And Stuff went down, to downtown Chicago, in the Loop, wherever it was, you know, with his violin. And he just started walking the halls out in front of Petrillo's office and started playing Italian songs.

He was way behind. He was about 10th on the list, you know? And so Petrillo says, 'Come here, Stuff.' He took him inside, you know, and the next thing the guy said Petrillo went to his bar and there was Stuff sitting on his desk, still playing these songs. He got his bargain. I said,
"Now that's another way to get it done."
Yeah, so, Stuff Smith was quite a -- he was something.
